summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with fever and right upper quadrant pressure due to a displaced percutaneous cholecystostomy tube and acute cholecystitis, in the setting of metastatic cholangiocarcinoma and recent antibiotic use. Imaging confirmed tube retraction and gallbladder inflammation. The drain was successfully replaced by interventional radiology. Cultures from bile grew multidrug-resistant E. coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was treated with IV tigecycline and oral ciprofloxacin, with improvement in symptoms and liver function. His chronic C. difficile prophylaxis with oral vancomycin was continued per infectious disease guidance. He remained afebrile, stable, and was discharged home with a plan to complete a 14-day antibiotic course via midline, ongoing drain care, and follow-up with radiology and oncology.
